summary: Discovery + poc scoping session focused on unit economics for inference. Covered workload sizing, expected QPS, batching and KV cache behavior, target latency SLOs, and budget constraints. Agreed to run a benchmark with customer sample prompts and produce per-token cost estimates and autoscaling suggestions.
transcript:
[00:00] John Miller: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, I'm John from Redwood inference, with Priya our solutions engineer. um Mark, Sarah, do you want to do quick intros?
[00:12] Mark Lambert: yeah hi i'm Mark, CTO at Quantum Ventures, we run financial risk models and want to add an LLM layer for analyst assistant.
[00:21] Sarah Cho: sarah - head of ML - i'm focused on production latencies and cost. we've been running some token-ops in house.
[00:30] Priya Shah: great, today we want to scope a POC: get your workload in, run benchmarks, measure per-token cost and latency tradeoffs, and validate caching/batching impact.
[00:45] John Miller: quick agenda - success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks & timelines, then next steps.
[00:53] Mark Lambert: sounds good. our main constraints: sub-300ms median latency for chat style queries, budget of around $12k/month for inference, and data residency concerns (us-east).
[01:07] Sarah Cho: also we care about tail latencies - 95th percentile - and ability to fall back to smaller model if cost spikes.
[01:15] Priya Shah: ok super, can we get a sense of QPS? average and peak?
[01:22] Ethan Park: currently avg QPS 2-3, peaks up to 18 during reporting windows - bursts last ~10-15 minutes.
[01:33] Priya Shah: good. that maps well to a small dedicated pool or hosted with burst routing. for cost modeling we'll need average prompt + response token counts - any ballpark?
[01:45] Sarah Cho: prompts average ~120 tokens, responses ~240 tokens, so ~360 tokens per request.
[01:54] John Miller: ok so baseline unit tokens ~360. rough per-token cost depends on model family and quantization. for example a 13b quantized variant on A100 class has ballpark $0.0008 per token for generation + context? that's a rough example.
[02:12] Mark Lambert: can you break that down? generation vs context vs embedding costs?
[02:17] Priya Shah: sure - typical split: context (the prompt) cost is cheaper because it's reading, generation cost scales with output length. caching (prefix/KV cache) can reduce repeated context cost a lot for multi-turn -- e.g., if you have repeated system prompt or few-shot examples we can cache KV and cut context compute by up to 60-70% on hits.
[02:35] Sarah Cho: our use-case is sessioned chat with long histories; how effective is KV cache for that?
[02:42] Priya Shah: depends on how much of the history is repeated. for persona/system + common reference prompts, high hit rate. for long unique user inputs, less. we usually recommend a hybrid: aggressive caching of static prefixes and shorter rolling context for recent history. that improves throughput and lowers per-token cost.
[02:59] John Miller: important knob is batching - continuous batching helps improve GPU utilization. if your latency SLO is tight (300ms) batching window size is small, so benefits are moderate. with slightly looser latency (500-700ms) you can batch more and reduce cost per token significantly.
[03:18] Mark Lambert: so trade-off is latency vs unit cost. can you give concrete numbers?
[03:23] Priya Shah: for your profile: if we target 300ms median, expected cost might be ~ $0.0009 per token; if we accept 600ms median, batching increases and cost drops to ~ $0.0005 per token. these are illustrative and we'll validate in the benchmark.
[03:39] Ethan Park: what's impact of quantization? we were considering int8.
[03:43] Priya Shah: int8 or 4-bit quant profiles typically reduce GPU memory and increase throughput. for 13B models int8 can cut cost ~20-40% depending on kernel performance. we also recommend running on a mixed fleet: cheaper quantized variant for background requests and full precision for high-fidelity outputs.
[04:00] Sarah Cho: regulatory question - logs and encryption. do you provide KMS integration and audit logs?
[04:05] John Miller: yes, Redwood Private supports customer KMS/HSM and detailed audit logs; hosted has SOC2 and encryption at rest, and we can provide whitepapers - we'll share the security pack.
[04:15] Mark Lambert: great. for the POC success criteria we'd define: 1) median latency <300ms for top 90% of sessions, 2) per-token cost < $0.0008 given current traffic, 3) no data exfiltration issues and acceptable encryption controls.
[04:30] Lina Torres: timeline: we want a pilot in 6 weeks. is that realistic?
[04:35] Priya Shah: yes. typical POC timeline: week 0-1 instrumentation & data share, week 2-3 benchmark runs and tuning, week 4-5 integration testing, week 6 review & decision.
[04:49] John Miller: next - benchmarks. we'll run two runs: throughput run to measure QPS at SLO targets and cost run to estimate per-token charge under your real prompts. please provide 10k representative prompts and traffic pattern.
[05:02] Mark Lambert: we can provide redacted prompts, and a CSV with timestamps for ramp patterns.
[05:07] Priya Shah: perfect. for the benchmark we'll include variants: 1) hosted default (higher perf GPUs), 2) dedicated reserved pool with quantized 13b, 3) fallback to smaller 7b for cost-sensitive flows.
[05:22] Sarah Cho: how long will each run take?
[05:25] Priya Shah: throughput runs typically 1-2 hours to capture variance; cost estimation runs use your sample set and a couple of stress windows - total ~3-4 hours.
[05:35] John Miller: we'll output a cost model spreadsheet with per-token breakdown: context read cost, generation cost, efficiency gains from batching, cache hit rates and effective per-request cost.
[05:47] Mark Lambert: can you include scheduled autoscaling cost? our budget must handle peak bursts.
[05:52] Priya Shah: yes - we'll model baseline reserved capacity and burst to hosted spare capacity. we'll show monthly cost for different commitment levels.
[06:01] Ethan Park: instrumenting metrics: what SDKs do you need?
[06:04] Priya Shah: simple HTTP/SDK calls and a Prometheus exporter for core metrics. we'll share a quickstart repo.
[06:12] John Miller: small note - transcription: sometimes our tools write KV cash instead of KV cache, ignore that.
[06:19] Mark Lambert: hahaha noted.
[06:22] Priya Shah: any blockers we haven't covered?
[06:25] Sarah Cho: one more: how do you measure quality regressions when switching to quantized or smaller models?
[06:31] Priya Shah: good point - we recommend an evaluation harness: run small eval prompt set and measure n-gram overlap, hallucination rates, and human-in-the-loop checks for a subset. Redwood Optimize provides regression alerts tied to your eval sets.
[06:46] Lina Torres: cost sensitivity - if cost exceeds target can we route low-risk requests to 7b?
[06:51] Priya Shah: absolutely - policy routing by route/intent is standard. you can tag intents as high/low fidelity and have automatic fallback.
[06:59] John Miller: recap: Redwood to run benchmark with 10k prompts; Priya to set up infra; John to send pricing model; customer to share traffic + success criteria; timeline target 6 weeks.
[07:13] Mark Lambert: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[07:16] John Miller: thanks, we'll follow up with calendar invites and the security pack + pricing sheet.
[07:22] Priya Shah: quick note on deliverables: benchmark report will include per-token table, latency SLO conformance, caching hit-rate assumptions and recommended autoscale policy.
[07:35] Sarah Cho: ok looking forward to the results.
[07:38] John Miller: thanks, end call.
